title: NY State Assembly · District 23
area: Southern Queens and the Rockaway peninsula, including Howard Beach, Ozone Park, Lindenwood, Broad Channel, Far Rockaway and Breezy Point.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Stacey Pheffer Amato is not seeking re-election. Pesach Osina defeated Mike Scala 60.6%-38.9% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary; Scala's separate "People Over Politics Party" ballot line was later invalidated, so he will not appear on the November ballot. Thomas Sullivan advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party primaries unopposed; he previously ran for this seat in 2024 and for NY State Senate District 15 in 2018.

candidates.name: Pesach Osina

summary.text: Pesach Osina is the Democratic and Community First Party nominee for the open NY State Assembly District 23 seat. He is a Rockaway resident and father of six who worked for years in government offices, including a Council Speaker's office, the city comptroller's office and a former Assembly member's district office, and who previously ran for City Council in 2013 and 2021. According to his campaign, he is focused on affordability, public safety and transportation in South Queens and the Rockaways.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, his parents owned and operated a nursing/elder-care business serving elderly residents; Osina describes them facing faith-based discrimination, which he says his father fought and won through the legal system.
Describes being elected student body president in college, where he says he built student leadership structures, and later becoming an entrepreneur who launched a catering and events business.

Worked for years in government offices: in the district for former Assemblymember Phil Goldfeder, for former Comptroller Scott Stringer, and for the past several years as lead senior liaison in the City Council Speaker's Office, according to the Queens Chronicle. The Queens Daily Eagle describes him as a longtime political staffer who worked in the City Council and the comptroller's office.

Was appointed by the Adams administration to the city Commission on Racial Equity, on which he serves according to the Queens Chronicle; the Chronicle reports he has focused on civil rights issues and combating hate crimes.

Ran for the City Council District 31 seat in a 2013 special election, finishing second to Donovan Richards, and again in a 2021 special election, losing to Selvena Brooks-Powers by about 1,200 votes, according to the Queens Daily Eagle.

Launched his Assembly campaign in January 2026 with the endorsement of outgoing Assemblymember Stacey Pheffer Amato, who has said she will not seek re-election. He won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over attorney Mike Scala, 60.6% to 38.9%, according to Ballotpedia.
Describes himself as politically moderate. Is a Rockaway resident and a father of six.

priorities.text: Affordability: pushing back on insurance and utility rate hikes, expanding tax relief for the middle class, and making childcare more affordable.
Public safety: strengthening retail-theft laws, holding repeat and organized theft offenders accountable, and giving law enforcement more tools.
Transportation: protecting the Cross Bay Bridge toll rebate, expanding Fair Fares, and advancing the QueensLink rail-reactivation project.

candidates.name: Thomas Sullivan

summary.text: Thomas Sullivan is the Republican, Conservative and We The People Party nominee for the open NY State Assembly District 23 seat. He is a retired U.S. Army Reserve colonel and financial-services professional who has run for office before: for NY State Senate District 15 in 2018 and 2020, and for this Assembly seat in 2022 and 2024. His 2024 Ballotpedia survey describes his platform as reducing crime, lowering taxes and cutting wasteful spending.

background.text: Was born in New York, New York, and the Queens Daily Eagle describes him as a native of Breezy Point. According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he is one of seven sons of a retired New York City Police detective and a nurse.

Grew up working in his family's restaurant, Brennan & Carr, in Brooklyn, and later opened a Brennan & Carr restaurant in Rockville Centre, NY, which he says employed 15-20 people; he says he also handles administrative matters for the family business.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1993) and a graduate degree (1996) from Mount Saint Mary's University, and a graduate degree from the U.S. Army War College (2018).

Served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 1993 to 2023. According to his survey, he commanded soldiers at the detachment, company, battalion and brigade levels during three combat deployments, and retired on June 1, 2023, as a colonel and deputy commanding officer of the 103rd Expeditionary Sustainment Command in Des Moines, Iowa.
Has worked as a financial consultant and financial-services professional for over three decades, according to his survey.

Ran for NY State Senate District 15 as the Republican nominee in 2018 (lost to incumbent Joseph Addabbo, 35.8% to 64.1%) and in 2020 (lost to Addabbo, 41.7% to 58.2%, also on the Conservative and Save Our City lines).

Ran for Assembly District 23 against incumbent Stacey Pheffer Amato in 2022 and 2024. The 2022 race was decided by 15 votes after a recount and legal challenges, according to the Queens Daily Eagle; Pheffer Amato won 2024 with 51.6% to his 48.2%, according to Ballotpedia.

Won the Republican and Conservative Party lines for 2026 without a primary, as both June 23 primaries were canceled. His survey lists affiliations with Veterans of Foreign Wars, the American Legion, the 77th Infantry Division Reserve Officers Association, Knights of Columbus, Ancient Order of Hibernians and Kiwanis.

priorities.text: Reducing crime, securing the border and enforcing immigration laws.
Lowering taxes and reducing what he calls wasteful government spending.
Addressing the high cost of living and quality-of-life issues he says are driving people out of New York.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he will fight to ensure local police have the resources they need and will work to secure funding for first responders.
positions.quote: Tom will fight to ensure our local police have the resources they need, invest in modern technology and equipment for law enforcement, and push to rebuild and modernize aging police precincts so our officers have safe, professional facilities to serve from.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from the Issues page of his campaign site (sullivanforstateassembly.com), plus his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (priorities). The campaign site is written in the third person. No prior officeholding record exists since he has not previously held elected office. No stance found on the other listed issues.
